cors.fact: CORS origin allowlist is loopback-only regex /^http:\/\/(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost)(:\d+)?$/ with credentials:false; desktop main process sends no Origin so it is unaffected; no browser-origin consumer found in website/ or apps/web (grep for api.neuropause033/PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL returned nothing)

body_limits.fact: express.json limit 256kb; urlencoded 256kb extended:false; /billing/webhook raw 1mb mounted before JSON parser for signature verification

rate_limits.fact: Per-IP fixed-window limiter (Redis INCR/EXPIRE) with in-process fallback when Redis is down (TD-3). Buckets: login 20/900s, register 10/3600s, password_reset 5/3600s, semantic_health 30/60s. No global limiter; /auth/token, /auth/token/refresh, /auth/logout, OAuth start/callback, /store, /organizations, /devices, /billing, /license, /sync, /memory/semantic search+backfill are NOT rate-limited.

trust_proxy.fact: No app.set('trust proxy') anywhere in apps/backend/src (grep 'trust proxy' -> 0 hits; grep x-forwarded-for|x-real-ip -> 0 hits). Caddy edge proxies with header_up X-Real-IP and the edge compose removes the backend's published port, so in the public deployment req.ip is the Caddy container address for every client.
trust_proxy.derived_consequence: DERIVED: all per-IP rate-limit buckets collapse into one shared key behind Caddy (one abuser exhausts login/register/reset budget for all users; brute-force protection is global not per-attacker); audit_log.ip (middleware/audit.ts:16) records the proxy IP.
